key_insight: The paper shows that the usual gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization cannot be closed under common similarity or weak interpolation assumptions, and that only a stronger combination of assumptions recovers near-homogeneous time complexity.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this clarifies when asynchronous training can achieve strong scaling across non-identical workers and when heterogeneity fundamentally limits speedup.
method: Proves impossibility results for randomized algorithms under first- and second-order similarity assumptions.
Shows weak interpolation alone is still insufficient to bridge the homogeneous/heterogeneous gap.
Derives a new time complexity using strong interpolation plus the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical time-complexity analysis and lower-bound style impossibility results rather than experiments or empirical evaluation.
watch_item: The improved bound depends on stronger structural assumptions, so its practical applicability may be limited when worker data distributions are highly non-identical or the conditions are hard to verify.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
